role: UX lead: visual systems and first-time comprehension combined. I am an AI reviewer. Nothing here is a user study; every claim is labeled MEASURED (simulated host), READ (code) or INFERRED.
environment:
Simulated host only. I used pi-sim.mjs from C:\Users\stephen\git\hwinfo-pi-density (production plugin-side modules from that working tree, which has uncommitted density-pass changes) with PI_SIM_PLUGIN_DIR set per build: proto-R, proto-A, the d04 reference, and my trial copy C:\Users\stephen\AppData\Local\Temp\hw-tfa-ux\proto-UX (R plus the UXR01 to UXR03 trials; the only edits are a tail block in ui/proto-R.css and two edits in ui/proto.js).

Browser: headless Chrome through cdp.mjs, run with npx tsx. Ports: 34210-34212 (R and trial), 34213-34215 (d04), 34216-34218 (A). DPR 1.5 at widths of 240 px and up, DPR 3 below, height 410. Widths: 373, 340, 320, 310, 300, 299, 280, 249, 220, 200, 199, 189, 175, 160.

States: key Default on Void, Paper, Ultraviolet, Graphite, Midnight and Forest; all 8 explicit picks; dial Ember; dial Default on Paper; empty key on Paper (folded directly, via a remembered fold, a reading picked while folded, then reopened and refolded); empty key with an unknown stored theme; empty dial on Void and Paper; unknown ids "neon-2031" and "synthwave-sunset-2027". Also: hover, focus-visible, Enter, Alt-click on the theme row, Fold all and Open all, Tab order on an explicit pick, and AX names from Accessibility.getPartialAXTree.

Late fold answer: sim.replyDelayMs also delays the themes payload, so chips cannot be focused before the answer. For the chip case, lab2.mjs patches ws send in-process to delay only the panelFolds answer by 700 ms.

Scripts: hw-tfa-ux\lab.mjs, lab2.mjs, sheet.py. Results: out\{R,A,d04}\lab.json and out2\{R,UX}\lab2.json. Contact sheets: sheets-chips-373.png, sheets-chips-160.png, sheets-states.png, sheets-empty.png, sheet-sbs-373.png, sheet-sbs-160.png, sheet-sbs-foldall.png, sheet-align.png. Read-only on the repo and every prototype dir. No Stream Deck app, HWiNFO, installed plugin, port 23654 or computer use.
summary:
R reads as one of the panel's sections in both states, and a first-time user can answer "what is drawn and where does it come from" in both states. I approve it with one small blocking alignment fix (UXR01, proven in my trial copy) and three non-blocking fixes.

Folded row (MEASURED):
- The row is 30 px against Reading's 30.2.
- "Theme" computes to 13px / 600 / rgb(236,236,236) at x 28, like Reading.
- The marker is 0 px off the title's center, and the gap after the title is 8 px.
- In Fold all, the six titles form one column and one rhythm. A's theme row is 34 px with the marker 2 px off.

Open row:
- It is d04's own line ("Theme Default (shared: Void) Change") with a fold marker. The title is bold, the name regular and the scope muted, so a d04 user sees the same words in the same place.
- Band height: 111 px against d04's 106.1 and A's 130 at 373.
- A shows "Theme" twice (a section row, then the band's label); R shows it once.

Comprehension in both states (MEASURED):
- The folded row keeps the same scope words as the open line. The chip carries the answer to "what is drawn": the name, the palette, and Default's dashed frame and link mark in the resolved palette.
- The AX name equals the visible words in both states: "Theme Default (shared: Void)", "Theme Ember (set on this key)", "Theme \"neon-2031\" (unknown; draws Void)", and on an empty key "... Shows on the key once a reading is picked."

The 24 px chip now reads as the chip, not a link (MEASURED plus RD):
- I measured 13 theme and shared combinations at 373 and 160. The stripe sits 3.9 px (Default) or 4.9 px (presets) under the baseline.
- Its gap to the word's line box is 1.1 px (Default) or 2.1 px (presets), identical to the grid chip's in every case.
- A's 22 px chip overlaps its line box by 0.9 to 1.9 px.
- Crops of all 8 chips (sheets-chips-373.png, sheets-chips-160.png) show a filled key face every time, never underlined text.
- The weakest edge is Graphite's face against the panel (1.24:1), and it still reads as a box at DPR 1.5.

The first-time-user reviewer's three reasons are answered:
1. The label-style title is now a section title (above).
2. The underline chip is now the grid chip's anatomy.
3. The empty-key fact now stays on the folded row, with Paper verified directly and via a remembered fold, at 373, 189 and 160, and in the AX name.

Attempts to break R (MEASURED):
- Pick stability: 8 picks on a key and a dial at 14 widths moved the chips 0 px. No line was cut and nothing overflowed.
- Near misses around Change fold nothing.
- Alt-click on the theme row folds every section.
- Tab order on an explicit pick is: row, checked chip, Reading.
- Clicking the folded chip opens the band.
- The late-answer guard keeps a focused summary and a focused chip open and focused (700 ms late answer, themes on time).

What I found:
1. UXR01 (blocking, small): when the line wraps, align-items: center floats "Theme" off its marker.
   - Folded, unknown id at 189 and 160: 13.2 to 21.6 px off (sheet-align.png).
   - Folded dial at 249: 4.8 px off.
   - Open, long unknown id at 373 and 320: 4.8 px off.
   - Open at 189 and 160: 2.9 px off.
   Six declarations fix every case (at most 0.1 px), and the known-theme heights and chip positions do not change.
2. UXR02: the empty-key note's held slot never releases. After a pick, reopening and refolding still leaves a blank line (47.1 px instead of 31).
3. UXR03: an empty key with an unknown stored theme loses the note.
4. UXR04: the "never folds" comments are still in the files (BT03).

Accepted deviation: at 200% zoom the open band is 247.6 px against d04's 216.7 and A's 240.6, and the row is 59.8 px against a11y's 42. That misses VT06's d04 + 8 budget. I accept it:
- It buys Change out of the row at every width.
- It keeps the two reserved lines, so no pick moves the chips.
- Folding at zoom gives 47.8 px, where d04's band stays at 216.7.

Residual for the owner (not a change): with focus in Reading when a late answer arrives, the band still folds and the focused field moves up 80 px, with focus kept (MEASURED). This already happens for every section and needs a fold reply slower than 300 ms.

round_one_blockers.id: BT01 (beginner): folded chip at the grid chip's geometry
round_one_blockers.evidence: MEASURED lab.json chips: the stripe-to-line-box gap is 1.1 px (Default) and 2.1 px (presets), identical to the grid chip in all 26 folded/grid pairs at 373 and 160. BT01 asks for at least 0.9 px and within 1 px of the grid; R is 0 px from the grid. The face is 24 px, not BT01's literal 30 px: R took VT03's 24 px anatomy, which passes BT01's own gap test. RD: sheets-chips-373.png and sheets-chips-160.png show the stripe clear of every word, including descenders (ink-to-stripe 1.9 px for Graphite, Midnight and Paper, the same as the grid). For comparison, A's 22 px chip measures -0.9 to -1.9 px.

changes.acceptance_test:
On the simulated host at 373, 320, 249, 189 and 160, open and folded, test six states: key Default on Void, dial Ember, key "neon-2031", key "synthwave-sunset-2027", empty key on Paper, and empty key with "neon-2031".
1. The fold marker's center (summary top + ::before top + 5) is within 1 px of the title's center.
2. Whenever the line or note wraps to a second visual line, its left edge is at x 28.
3. No horizontal overflow.
4. The 8-pick sweep on a key and a dial with shared Ultraviolet at 373, 340, 320, 310, 300, 299, 249, 189 and 160 gives one chip top per width, equal to R's: 121/137, 133.6, 194.1, 210.2, 278.1/262.1, 294.2/262.1.
5. Summary heights stay 30 px open at 300 and up, and 59.8 px open under 300. The folded band stays 31 px at 280 and up, and 47.8 px at 189 and 160.

The trial passes all five (lab2.mjs UX run).

changes.change: The empty-key note's held slot lasts only while the band stays folded. The next time the band opens with the note empty, drop the hold. Trial in proto-UX ui/proto.js: a 'toggle' listener on #sec-theme that, when details.open and the note is empty, clears noteHeld and re-syncs. In production this lives in the same render that fills the note.
changes.why:
MEASURED (out2/R/lab2.json emptyHold, sheets-empty.png): after a reading is picked on a folded empty key, R keeps a blank line in the folded row for the rest of the panel's life. Refolded, the band is still 47.1 px instead of 31. After Fold all it is still 47.1. A newcomer sees an unexplained gap under 'Theme [chip] (shared: Paper)'.

The hold exists so the first reading moves nothing under the pointer. Once the band has been opened, the fold itself moves everything, so the hold has no job left. MEASURED in the trial: the pick still moves Reading 0 px (136.1 before and after).
changes.acceptance_test:
Setup: key-empty on a Paper shared theme at 373, band folded (47.1 px).
1. Push a reading: the band stays 47.1 px and #sec-reading's top moves 0 px.
2. Open the band, then fold it: the band is 31 px and #theme-note's height is 0.
3. Repeat the pick, then use Open all and Fold all: 31 px.

The trial measured 47.1, then 47.1 with 0 px move, then 31, then 31. R measures 47.1 at the last two steps.

changes.change: Drive the folded note from the same test that sets the help line, !configured && kind === "key" in renderThemeHelp, as BT02 asked. Do not use chip presence or a match on the help text (proto.js line 34 requires chip !== null and matches /^Shows on the key/). Then an empty key with an unknown stored theme also carries the note.
changes.why: MEASURED: key-empty with settings.theme "neon-2031" folds to 'Theme "neon-2031" (unknown; draws Void)' with no note. The row claims Void, while the empty key draws its fixed black 'Pick a sensor' prompt. The open help for that key does say 'Shows on the key once a reading is picked.' (READ renderThemeHelp: the no-reading text wins over the unknown text), so R shows the fact open and drops it folded. The state is rare, but it is the same truth gap as BT02.
changes.acceptance_test:
1. key-empty with theme "neon-2031", folded: the AX name reads 'Theme "neon-2031" (unknown; draws Void) Shows on the key once a reading is picked.' The band is at most 47 px at 373 (the trial measured 46.1), with no overflow at 160.
2. dial-empty with an unknown theme, folded: no note.
3. Configured keys: no note.

changes.why: READ in proto-R: all four still state the retired rule, next to markup that now folds. The next reader could take a relaxed owner rule for a live one and 'fix' the fold back out.
changes.acceptance_test: grep -rn "never fold" com.lawrensen.hwinfo.sdPlugin/ui returns no line about the theme band or palette.

keep: The theme line itself is the fold row. Open, it is d04's line plus a marker: 111 px against d04's 106.1 and A's 130 at 373. Folded, the chip takes the name's slot and the scope stays: 31 px.
One section row: 30 px against Reading's 30.2; title 13px/600/#ececec at x 28; marker 0 px off; 8 px after the title. Fold all shows one column of six titles (A: 34 px, marker 2 px off).
Name at weight 400 with a muted scope. The open line reads title, value, scope.

The 24 px folded chip with the grid chip's anatomy: stripe-to-line-box gap identical to the grid chip in all 26 measured pairs; Default's dashed frame and link mark in the resolved palette; no selection ring; not focusable. Clicking it opens the band.
Change outside the row: the row ends 13.5 px before it. Hover and focus stop before Change when open and span the full row when folded. At zoom, Change sits on its own line, right-aligned.
Two reserved name lines at zoom: 8 picks move the chips 0 px at 14 widths on a key and a dial. The accepted cost is 247.6 px open at 200% zoom.
Never ellipsized: an unknown id folds to text only, '"id" (unknown; draws X)', with the full id in the AX name.
The empty-key note on the folded row and in the AX name, with no note on dials, and 0 px movement when the first reading lands.
Open all, Fold all and Alt-click include the band (Alt-click on the theme row folds all, MEASURED). Folds are remembered per panel kind, and the band stays hidden until the fold answer arrives.
The shell guard: a late fold answer never folds a section holding focus. MEASURED for a focused summary and a focused chip, with a 700 ms answer and the themes on time.
#theme-desc hidden: it stays the radiogroup's description without a duplicate StaticText.
